question: A drug with a seemingly monocompartmental distribution pattern is administered in the form of i.v. perfusion. at a constant speed of 20 mg / h for 48 h. Once the perfusion is finished, three blood samples are taken, which, when analyzed, allow the calculation of the primary parameters of the model Kel = 0.0495 h-1, concentration at the end of the perfusion (C48h) = 5,553 μg / mL, Vd = 66 L. At what time would the steady state be reached ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Drug administered intravenously -> Constant speed perfusion -> Blood samples taken after 48 hours -> Primary parameters calculated: Kel = 0.0495 h-1, C48h = 5,553 μg/mL, Vd = 66 L -> Steady state reached when rate of drug administration equals rate of elimination -> Steady state reached after approximately 4-5 half-lives -> Kel = 0.0495 h-1, so half-life (t1/2) = ln(2) / Kel = 13.98 hours -> Steady state reached after 4-5 half-lives -> Steady state reached after 56-70 hours -> Answer: opd. 56 h. -> 90%
enhanced_information: The drug administered intravenously at a constant speed of 20 mg/h for 48 hours follows a monocompartmental distribution pattern. The primary parameters calculated indicate a Kel of 0.0495 h-1, C48h of 5,553 μg/mL, and Vd of 66 L. The steady state is reached when the rate of drug administration equals the rate of elimination, typically after 4-5 half-lives. With a half-life of approximately 13.98 hours, the steady state would be reached after 56-70 hours. Therefore, the correct answer is opd. 56 h.
